An unauthenticated attacker can create arbitrary pastes (including private and burn-after-reading), polluting the paste database.

metadata.proof: SOURCE: The createUser mutation (line 92) has no throttling, CAPTCHA, or account-creation lockout. SINK: User.create_user(...) inserts into the users table with no rate check. An attacker can automate registration requests to mass-create accounts and fill the database, and combine with username enumeration from the login oracle.

extra.message: User Enumeration via CreateUser Duplicate-Key Error

metadata.proof: Untrusted input user_data.username and user_data.email flow from CreateUser.mutate (core/views.py:99-106) into User.create_user (core/models.py:17-21). The db.session.commit() at line 20 triggers a SQLAlchemy IntegrityError when a UNIQUE constraint on username or email is violated. No exception handling exists in either create_user or CreateUser.mutate, so the raw IntegrityError message (e.g., 'UNIQUE constraint failed: users.username') propagates through format_custom_error to the GraphQL response. An attacker can probe for existing accounts by observing whether the mutation succeeds or returns a constraint-violation error.
